title: Social Security Number Fraud Prevention Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on May 24, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Social Security Number Fraud Prevention Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill: (1) prohibits federal agencies (including legislative and judicial branch agencies, with specified exceptions) from including any individual's Social Security account number on any document sent by mail unless the agency head determines that such inclusion is necessary; and (2) requires agencies that have Chief Financial Officers to issue regulations, within five years of this bill's enactment, that specify the circumstances under which such inclusion is necessary.

summary.headline: A 2017 federal law limits federal agencies from putting Social Security numbers on mailed documents unless the agency head finds it necessary.
summary.what_it_does: Federal agencies, including those in the legislative and judicial branches with some exceptions, generally may not include a person's Social Security account number on documents sent by mail. An agency head can still allow it if they decide it is necessary. Agencies that have Chief Financial Officers must issue rules within five years of enactment that describe when including the number is necessary.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive mail from federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: Agencies should less often print their full Social Security number on letters and other documents sent to them by mail.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that send mail to the public
who_it_affects.how: They must stop including Social Security numbers on mailed documents unless the agency head determines it is necessary.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies with Chief Financial Officers
who_it_affects.how: They must write regulations within five years of enactment that explain the circumstances in which including a Social Security number on mail is necessary.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on September 15, 2017; the required agency regulations are due within five years of that date, and the summary does not give a separate start date for the mailing limit.
